newsitem.title: USA: Investigation into Corning's Damon ongoing.
newsitem.headline: Investigation into Corning's Damon ongoing.

text.p: The U.S. government's investigation into Corning Inc unit Damon Clinic Laboratories is continuing and the government may consider criminal charges against corporate executives, U.S. Attorney Donald Stern said.
Corning, which bought Damon in August 1993 for about $370 million, cooperated with the investigation and no employees at Corning will be charged, Stern told reporters at a press conference in Boston.
Corning guaranteed to pay a $119 million fine levied Wednesday against Damon, Stern said.
"When Corning purchased Damon, the practice stopped," Stern said. Corning has since established a model compliance program, he added.
Corning announced earlier it would take a charge of $115 million in the third quarter, most of it to cover the fine, spokeswoman Kathy Littleton told Reuters.
Littleton said the fine will have no impact on Corning's plan to spin off its clinical laboratory business, Corning Clinical Laboratories, as planned before year-end.
Damon no longer conducts business, Littleton said.
The settlement represents $35.273 million in criminal fines and $83.7 million in civil liabilities.

Stern said the criminal fine is the largest ever levied in the healthcare field in the United States and is the largest ever in any case ever brought by the federal government in the state of Massachusetts.

In reaction to declining profits and a changing healthcare marketplace, Damon decided to cheat the Medicare program, Stern alleged. Between January 1988 and August 1993, Damon submitted to federal and state healcare programs millions of fradulent claims for payment for medically unnecessary laboratory tests, he said.
Stern said the government fined Damon $3 for every $1 the company overcharged healthcare programs.
